title: Edmund and the Ember
premise: Petra Vasquez, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has spent her life in a valley where magic cannot follow—until Edmund, a mute child who speaks a language older than kingdoms, arrives at her door with a stolen ember burning in his chest. The ember is a soul: sold by Edmund's desperate parents to the court beneath the mountain, and Petra's oath compels her to carry it home before it gutters out. Descending through a world where her sword-magic finally wakes, she discovers the court's Ember King has been harvesting souls to hold back his own unraveling—and that her valley was built as his prison, not her sanctuary. In the end Petra must choose between restoring the oath that defines her and shattering it, trading her own name into the ember so Edmund can live free above ground.
about_author: Vesper Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval oaths and contracts before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people bound by promises they no longer believe in.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Establishes daily life in the magic-dead valley: her ritual maintenance of a sword she cannot draw, the villagers' quiet distrust, and the anniversary of her oath. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as duty.

chapters.title: A Knock at Dusk
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A child appears at her door during a storm, barefoot, unafraid, speaking syllables that make her sword hum for the first time in years. He carries no shadow. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into recognition.

chapters.title: The Word That Opens Doors
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She realizes Edmund's language is Oathscript—the tongue swordspeakers used to bind magic. When he speaks one word, her blade draws itself an inch from its sheath. Emotional beat: terror and longing entwined.

chapters.title: What the Village Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with the miller's widow, Maren. The village elders demand the boy be given to the border wardens; Maren defends him, revealing fragments of Petra's own arrival decades ago. Emotional beat: belonging revealed as fragile consensus.

chapters.title: The Ember in His Chest
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At night Edmund's chest glows like banked coals; touching it, Petra hears a voice—not his—begging in her mother's dialect. She understands: this is a sold soul, and her oath names her its keeper. Emotional beat: dread of obligation accepted.

chapters.title: Terms of the Sale
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, fragmentary and dreamlike. Memories of parents, a hooded broker, a contract signed in ash. He remembers choosing to swallow the ember to keep it from the King's men. Emotional beat: child courage masking grief.

chapters.title: Wardens at the Ford
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Border wardens arrive hunting the escaped soul. Petra lies for the first time since her oath, and the valley's protective silence flickers—the wards know. Emotional beat: guilt as first crack in identity.

chapters.title: Leaving the Quiet
chapters.summary: Petra and Edmund slip out at dawn past the boundary stones. Crossing the line, sound returns, color sharpens, and Petra's sword sings fully awake for the first time. Emotional beat: vertigo of a self unbound.

chapters.title: The Road Sings Back
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Outside the valley, every spoken word carries weight; Edmund's speech bends small fortunes. Petra teaches him guard-words while learning how rusty her own craft is. Emotional beat: awkward joy of apprenticeship reversed.

chapters.title: Hollowbridge Market
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a trade town they seek a translator of Oathscript and find instead a bounty notice bearing Edmund's likeness—and Petra's old name beneath it. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Translator's Price
chapters.summary: New character POV: Sefa, a disgraced court scribe. She agrees to translate Edmund's words for a favor owed to someone below the mountain. Emotional beat: transactional kindness hiding a hook.

chapters.title: What the Boy Says
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Translation reveals Edmund's message: 'The ember is my sister. Carry her home or the King eats the light.' Petra learns the soul is Edmund's sister Liss, sold whole. Emotional beat: horror reframing the quest.

chapters.title: Riders in Ash Cloaks
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The King's harvesters ambush them on the moor road. Petra draws her sword fully for the first time and discovers her speech-blades still work—but each word costs memory. Emotional beat: power as slow self-erasure.

chapters.title: The Cost Counted
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, quiet interlude. She catalogs what she's forgotten already: a face, a birthday, the taste of bread. Edmund watches her pay. Emotional beat: tenderness shadowed by arithmetic.

chapters.title: Maren Follows
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The widow catches up, having abandoned the valley herself after forty years of fear, carrying supplies and a map drawn by Petra's vanished mentor. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Map
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The map shows the mountain's true shape: not a fortress but a mouth, and the valley marked as 'the seal.' Petra realizes her sanctuary was a lock, and she was left as its key. Emotional beat: betrayal by the dead.

chapters.title: City of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They reach Grayharbor, where all debts are recorded—including soul-contracts. To void Liss's sale they need the original ledger page. Emotional beat: hope requiring theft.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Hall of Debts
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa leads them inside using her revoked credentials; Edmund's language unlocks doors that predate the city. Emotional beat: competence and camaraderie mid-heist.

chapters.title: The Page That Bleeds
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They find Liss's contract—signed not by Edmund's parents alone but countersigned by a swordspeaker's mark. Petra recognizes her own hand, aged backward. Emotional beat: identity shaken to the root.

chapters.title: Interrogating Herself
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sefa deciphers the countersignature: a future-tense oath, meaning Petra will sign it below the mountain. Every step forward is a step toward becoming the traitor in the record. Emotional beat: fatalism versus defiance.

chapters.title: The Harvesters Return
chapters.summary: Action chapter, Petra's POV. Ash-cloaks corner them on the harbor wall; Maren is taken instead of Edmund when he freezes. Petra's rescue fails. Emotional beat: failure with a hostage price.

chapters.title: Parley With a Warden of Souls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A harvester captain offers terms: deliver the ember voluntarily and Maren lives, and Petra may keep her memories. Petra refuses—and loses something anyway. Emotional beat: moral cost made explicit.

chapters.title: Edmund Speaks Plainly
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Trauma cracks his Oathscript muteness; he tells Petra plainly that he swallowed the ember because he couldn't save Liss, and asks if Petra will fail too. Emotional beat: raw honesty between child and guardian.

chapters.title: The Ascent to the Mouth
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The company climbs the mountain's throat through galleries of harvested souls dimming in niches like votive lamps. Emotional beat: awe curdling into grief.

chapters.title: Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They enter the Ember Court, beautiful and starving, where nobles wear borrowed light. The Ember King greets Petra by name—and by her future title. Emotional beat: seduction of a gilded cage.

chapters.title: The King's Unraveling
chapters.summary: Ember King's POV. He shows Petra the truth: he is the valley's original prisoner, consuming souls to keep the seal intact, and the valley's peace was purchased with his endless hunger. Emotional beat: villainy as tragic necessity.

chapters.title: Liss Among the Lamps
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They find Liss's soul half-harvested, flickering. Edmund reaches for her; the contract activates, demanding a countersignature to release her. Emotional beat: love meeting legal trap.

chapters.title: The Signing Table
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The table waits with pen and ash. Petra understands the loop: she signs, becomes the betrayer of record, and the cycle renews. Emotional beat: choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Refusal in Oathscript
chapters.summary: Climax begins, Petra's POV. Instead of signing, Petra speaks a counter-oath in full Oathscript, offering her own name and memories as collateral to void the sale. Her sword drinks her history word by word. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: The Sword Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Freed from Petra's erasure, the blade becomes a vessel of every forgotten thing—including the valley's founding lie. The court reels as truth-light floods the galleries. Emotional beat: revelation as weapon.

chapters.title: The Seal Broken From Inside
chapters.summary: Climax, Petra's POV. Petra shatters the valley-seal rather than renew it, freeing the Ember King to dissolve rather than feed. He chooses, at the last, to spend himself lighting every lamp-niche. Emotional beat: mercy for the monstrous.

chapters.title: Liss Rekindled
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Liss's soul, freed, cannot return to flesh—but can rest. Edmund says goodbye in plain words and Oathscript both. Emotional beat: grief honored, not fixed.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Falling Light
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The mountain goes dark and quiet; the company descends carrying lamps lit by the King's last spending. Petra cannot remember her own name—but knows Edmund's. Emotional beat: hollow victory, warm hands.

chapters.title: The Empty Valley
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They return to find the valley waking, magic seeping in, villagers frightened and free. Some flee; some stay. Maren claims a house and plants a garden over the boundary stones. Emotional beat: ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Naming What Was Lost
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Nameless, Petra lets Edmund choose what to call her. He calls her 'Keeper,' reclaiming the word from the oath that broke her. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt by love rather than law.

chapters.title: Sefa's Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa burns her debt-page and stays in the valley as its first new teacher of Oathscript, teaching children words that open nothing and mean everything. Emotional beat: redemption through service.

chapters.title: The Ember Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A sliver of Liss's light remains in Edmund's chest—not a debt now, a keepsake. Petra teaches him the first guard-word properly, apprentice and master at once. Emotional beat: inheritance without burden.

chapters.title: Doors Left Open
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. Travelers begin arriving at the valley—a world remade needs witnesses. Petra, nameless and unbound, greets them at the door where Edmund once arrived. Emotional beat: the circle turned outward.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Ember
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, closing mirror of chapter two. Years later, Edmund stands at the boundary as a young swordspeaker, ember-warm, watching a storm roll in—and hears a knock. Emotional beat: continuity, welcome, and the story handing itself on.
